original_value: Visual object tracking is an important research topic in the field of computer vision. Tracking–learning–detection (TLD) decomposes the tracking problem into three modules—tracking, learning, and detection—which provides effective ideas for solving the tracking problem. In order to improve the tracking performance of the TLD tracker, three improvements are proposed in this paper. The built-in tracking module is replaced with a kernelized correlation filter (KCF) algorithm based on the histogram of oriented gradient (HOG) descriptor in the tracking module. Failure detection is added for the response of KCF to identify whether KCF loses the target. A more specific detection area of the detection module is obtained through the estimated location provided by the tracking module. With the above operations, the scanning area of object detection is reduced, and a full frame search is required in the detection module if objects fails to be tracked in the tracking module. Comparative experiments were conducted on the object tracking benchmark (OTB) and the results showed that the tracking speed and accuracy was improved. Further, the TLD tracker performed better in different challenging scenarios with the proposed method, such as motion blur, occlusion, and environmental changes. Moreover, the improved TLD achieved outstanding tracking performance compared with common tracking algorithms.

result.paraphrase: Visual object tracking is a key research area in computer vision. Tracking–learning–detection (TLD) breaks the tracking task into three parts—tracking, learning, and detection—offering effective ideas for solving it. To enhance TLD tracking performance, this paper proposes three improvements: the original tracking module is replaced by a kernelized correlation filter (KCF) algorithm based on the histogram of oriented gradients (HOG) descriptor; failure detection is added to the KCF response to determine whether the target has been lost; and the detection module uses the estimated location from the tracking module to define a more precise search region. These changes reduce the object-detection scanning area, while a full-frame search is triggered in the detection module when tracking fails. Experiments on the object tracking benchmark (OTB) show improved speed and accuracy. The proposed method also makes the TLD tracker perform better in challenging scenarios such as motion blur, occlusion, and environmental changes, and the improved TLD delivers excellent tracking results compared with common tracking algorithms.
